title: Which food is nearer to the hungry rabbit?
description: Meera's rabbit sits at a number on a garden path with food on both sides. The video counts the jumps each way and picks the food with fewer jumps.
teaching_notes: One idea: the nearest ten is the one with fewer jumps, found by taking away both ways. Watch for a child who picks a food because it comes first or looks familiar.

source: The rabbit is at 2,346 and its food is at 2,340 and 2,350. W
video_script.why: The child knows tens on a number line, but has not yet decided which ten a number is nearest to.
video_script.substitution: Count the jumps up and down to the two tens and choose the fewer.
video_script.anchor: Meera's pet rabbit hopping along a numbered garden path in Pune
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu picks the smaller food because it comes first. Only the number of jumps tells which food is near.
video_script.payoff_line: four jumps is fewer than six jumps

final_answer.value: 2,350 is the nearest ten of 2,346, with 4 jumps
final_answer.spoken: two thousand three hundred and fifty with four jumps

maths_rules: your turn: rabbit at 6,572, food at 6,570 and 6,580; 6,572 − 6,570 = 2 and 6,580 − 6,572 = 8; 2 < 8 so 6,570; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: the fewer jumps win. The rabbit and path stay as the anchor; the number line and the two counts build on the stage and working areas.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='rabbit'/>Meera's hungry rabbit sits on a garden path in Pune. It is at two thousand three hundred and forty six.
<bookmark mark='food'/>Food waits at two thousand three hundred and forty. More food waits at two thousand three hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which food does the rabbit reach in the fewest jumps?

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>Look at the path between the two foods.
<bookmark mark='jump'/>Each jump moves the rabbit to the next number on the path.
<bookmark mark='def'/>The ten with the fewest jumps is called the nearest ten.

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>The rabbit goes to the smaller food, because that food comes first.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Coming first does not make a food near.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Count the jumps to each food before you choose.

marks.up: the jumps up are drawn on the line

narration: <bookmark mark='up'/>Count the jumps up to the food on the right.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>Two thousand three hundred and fifty take away two thousand three hundred and forty six leaves four.

marks.down: the jumps down are drawn on the line
marks.pay: 4 and 6 glow side by side and the bowl at 2,350 is lit; the card 2,350 is the nearest ten appears

narration: <bookmark mark='down'/>Next, count the jumps down to the food on the left.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>Two thousand three hundred and forty six take away two thousand three hundred and forty leaves six.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Four jumps is fewer than six jumps, so the rabbit goes to two thousand three hundred and fifty.

<bookmark mark='food'/>Food waits at six thousand five hundred and seventy, and at six thousand five hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='q'/>Which is the nearest ten?
